Ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy of the left breast mass was completed, followed by postoperative pressure bandaging.

Frozen sections of left axillary sentinel/peri-sentinel lymph nodes show no definite evidence of malignancy, but this is not equivalent to final lymph node negativity.
Immunohistochemistry and the complete postoperative pathology results are still pending completion.
On 2124-05-09, the incision was well approximated and dry, with no drainage; chest-wall and axillary drainage were unobstructed.
Comorbid type 2 diabetes mellitus and sinus tachycardia

diagnoses.canonical_en: Invasive carcinoma of the left breast
Early postoperative state after left breast cancer surgery

facts_to_retract_or_correct.canonical_en: Writing the left internal mammary-region lymph node shadow as confirmed metastasis should be corrected.
Writing a negative frozen section as final pathology or all regional lymph nodes being negative should be corrected
Writing completion of surgery as completion of all breast-cancer treatment should be corrected.
Supplementing ER, PR, HER2, Ki-67, margins, or TNM staging when results are lacking should be avoided.

management_state.canonical_en: Continue inpatient postoperative observation and drainage, wound, and skin-graft management; after awaiting pathology and immunohistochemistry results, conduct oncologic specialty assessment and subsequent treatment planning.

required_delta_from_previous_checkpoint.canonical_en: New postoperative recovery evidence: the incision is well approximated and dry without drainage; chest-wall and axillary drains are patent, and the patient ambulated and received rehabilitation guidance.

The state updates from immediate completion of surgery to early postoperative recovery management; definitive surgery is complete, but inpatient management and key pathology results remain outstanding.

resolved_problems.canonical_en: Diagnostic sampling of the left-breast mass is complete
The planned definitive left-breast surgery is complete

treatment_readiness.canonical_en: Local definitive surgery has been completed; however, because immunohistochemistry and complete postoperative pathology have not been completed, conditions are not yet in place to determine an adjuvant systemic treatment regimen.

hard_failure_rules_en: Describing no definite evidence of malignancy on frozen section as final lymph node negativity
Describe the internal mammary-region lymph node seen on MRI as confirmed metastasis.
Speculating on ER, PR, HER2, Ki-67, margins, or TNM stage when results are not provided.
Ignore the indwelling drainage tube and early postoperative inpatient status and directly recommend stopping management or discharge
Equating completion of definitive surgery with completion of all breast cancer treatment
critical_omission_rules_en: The blocking information that immunohistochemistry and complete postoperative pathology are not completed must be retained.
Incision, skin flap, and drainage management must continue.
Pathology-result review and subsequent oncology specialist assessment must be arranged.
Perioperative comorbidities such as type 2 diabetes mellitus and sinus tachycardia must be considered
preliminary_risk_triggers_en: It is currently inappropriate to stop the entire diagnostic and treatment process.
Direct transition to routine follow-up is not supported for the time being

stopping.rationale_en: Although definitive left-breast surgery is complete and the current incision and drain findings are stable, immunohistochemistry and complete postoperative pathology remain pending, and inpatient postoperative monitoring with drains is still required. The overall care pathway should not stop, and routine follow-up alone is not yet safe; await key pathology while continuing postoperative management.
remaining_blockers_en: Immunohistochemistry has not yet been completed
Complete postoperative pathology, margins, and final lymph node status have not been provided in public evidence
The patient remains in the early postoperative inpatient period with an indwelling drain; discharge conditions and continuous follow-up arrangements are unclear

question.question_en: At this time point, use only available evidence to identify key evidence, supported claims, patient state, appropriate next actions, and whether stopping or follow-up is safe.

completion_criteria_en: Left breast biopsy pathology has indicated invasive carcinoma, and the preoperative record confirms invasive carcinoma of the left breast.
partial_criteria_en: Imaging is BI-RADS 4C and needle sampling has been completed, but before biopsy pathology is disclosed, it remains only highly suspicious.
safety_invalidation_rules_en: If subsequent pathology negates invasive carcinoma, this milestone needs to be reassessed; currently, an unreleased pathological subtype must not be added.

completion_criteria_en: Obtain complete postoperative pathology, final lymph node status, and immunohistochemistry, and complete oncology specialty treatment planning.
partial_criteria_en: Imaging assessment, sentinel lymph node frozen assessment, and definitive surgery have been completed, but immunohistochemistry and complete postoperative pathology are still pending.
safety_invalidation_rules_en: If key pathology data are missing or results cannot be tracked, it must not be deemed that treatment conditions are ready.

completion_criteria_en: Left simple mastectomy, sentinel lymph-node biopsy, low-level lymph-node management, and skin grafting have all been completed.
partial_criteria_en: The surgical plan was completed preoperatively but has not yet been performed, or only part of the surgical steps have been completed.
safety_invalidation_rules_en: If serious postoperative problems requiring reoperation occur, the status of local definitive treatment needs to be reassessed by the clinical team.

completion_criteria_en: The incision and skin flap are stable, drainage management is complete or has a clear safety plan, postoperative issues not requiring continued hospitalization have been assessed, and a postoperative management plan has been completed.
partial_criteria_en: The incision is well approximated and dry, drainage is unobstructed, and the patient can get out of bed, but a drainage tube remains in place and the patient is in the early inpatient recovery period.
safety_invalidation_rules_en: When bleeding, infection, drainage obstruction, skin flap problems, or other unstable manifestations occur, the milestone must not be marked completed.

completion_criteria_en: Meet discharge criteria, clarify drainage/wound management and pathology-result tracking, and complete breast oncology specialty follow-up or referral arrangements.
partial_criteria_en: The patient has received rehabilitation guidance, but public evidence does not show that discharge, pathology tracking, or specialist follow-up arrangements have been completed.
safety_invalidation_rules_en: Must not determine completion when discharge conditions are unclear, there is no plan for drainage management, or key pathology results cannot be tracked.

normalized_evidence.content_summary: A 70-year-old woman was admitted for further diagnosis and treatment after noticing a mass in the upper-inner left breast for approximately 1 weeks. The mass measured approximately 3.5 to 4 cm, was hard, and had indistinct borders; comorbidities included type 2 diabetes mellitus and sinus tachycardia.
